title: A Uniform for the Regiment
premise: In 1847, Xanthe Ashgrove has spent two decades as a battlefield nurse in the garrison town of Marrow's Ford, quietly recording in a hidden ledger the names of soldiers the officers' official reports omit—the deserters shot, the dead listed as missing, the men erased to protect reputations. When the army requisitions the town and orders all records surrendered, Xanthe must smuggle the ledger past three checkpoints before the spring ice breaks on the river, aided by Captain Elias Vane, the one officer whose brother's name fills its pages. At the final checkpoint, Elias must choose between his commission and the truth, and he burns his own uniform papers to create the diversion that lets Xanthe cross. The book ends with the ledger published and the river breaking, as Xanthe finally speaks the names aloud at a public inquiry—no longer invisible, but no longer safe either.
about_author: Petra Brightwater is the pen name of a former archivist who spent years cataloguing military correspondence and became obsessed with the gaps between official reports and private letters. She writes historical fiction from a converted ferry house on a cold northern river.

chapters.title: The Weight of Omitted Names
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Opening in the military hospital during a bitter winter, Xanthe tends dying soldiers and adds three new names to his hidden ledger after an officer's report conveniently lists them as 'deserted.' The army arrives with requisition orders for the town and every record within it. Emotional beat: quiet dread hardening into resolve as Xanthe realizes twenty years of careful silence are about to be searched.

chapters.title: What the Captain Remembers
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Xanthe and Captain Elias Vane, assigned to inventory the hospital's records. Elias discovers a page referencing his brother, officially 'lost with honor,' actually executed for mutiny. He confronts Xanthe, who shows him the ledger rather than lie. Emotional beat: wary alliance formed in guilt and grief; both understand the other is risking everything by trusting a stranger.

chapters.title: Three Checkpoints
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV, tense and propulsive. With the ice groaning on the river, Xanthe sews ledger pages into his nurse's apron and moves through the occupied town: bribing a drunk sergeant at the mill checkpoint, bluffing past a childhood acquaintance now a provost at the bridge, then being recognized at the final gate. Elias intervenes, burning his own commission papers to spark a diversionary fire. Emotional beat: terror sharpened by love neither will name aloud.

chapters.title: When the Ice Breaks
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, resolution. Xanthe crosses the river as it fractures, reaching the magistrate's office across the border; Elias is court-martialed but spared when the ledger's evidence forces a public inquiry. In the final scene, Xanthe reads the names aloud while Elias watches from the gallery in civilian clothes. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into testimony—truth costs everything, and is worth it.
